question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for this request: deny-wins `tools.fs.allowedPaths`/`denyPaths`, access-mode `tools.fs.roots`, or a narrower workspace-only plus separate exec policy split?
rationale: This defines a public config surface and security boundary, and current open implementation candidates make different compatibility and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate tracker
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels clearly state that shell-mediated file access remains a separate security boundary.

options.title: Defer to OS or container isolation
options.body: Reject additional host path ACLs only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own filesystem path policy beyond workspaceOnly and sandbox backends.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current schema/tool-policy history and already framed the previous keep-open review for this security boundary.
